title: Market Valuation and Acquisition Quality: Empirical Evidence

rival_explanations: market valuation simply proxying for firm (acquirer) valuation
hidden premium from targets being overvalued in high-valuation markets
market timing (exploiting overvalued stock) rather than deal quality
industry effect (early and late movers in different industries)
overpayment by late acquirers due to targets in short supply
differences in acquirer or target characteristics (leftover targets)

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (U.S. publicly traded firms; industry effects controlled via the 17 Fama-French industry groupings)
context.country_region: United States (acquirers are U.S. firms listed on NYSE, NASDAQ, or AMEX)
context.sample_description: Completed tender offers and mergers from the SDC US Mergers and Acquisitions Database; target not a subsidiary; transaction value ≥ $50 million; acquirer obtains at least 50% of target shares; acquirer prior-month closing price ≥ $3; payment in cash, stock, or a mix

data_sources.name: equally weighted CRSP index (daily and monthly acquirer return data)
Compustat (EBITDA = Compustat #13; average total assets = Compustat #6)
P/E data on Bob Shiller's Web site (www.irrationalexuberance.com)
